_comment: Every imagery tile any venue derives a claim from, pinned the way this package already pins assets (data/display/assets.json) and reference images (data/display/references/images.json). Read by lib/imagery-ledger.mjs. Rows are recorded as the venue's sources.json actually stamps them; a row is never edited to make a gate pass, and there is no exemption field. A row that raises problems is an open question for a human, not a bug in the ledger.

okaloosa-ortho-2025.label: Okaloosa County 2025 orthophotography over Big Kahuna's Destin
okaloosa-ortho-2025.used_for: Walking paths OpenStreetMap does not draw, and ride positions where OSM names geometry but not the attraction.
okaloosa-ortho-2025.review: UNADJUDICATED — the question sharpened, it did not close. Re-recorded from the venue's corrected sources.json, not edited to pass a gate: the row still fails, and should. (a) The owner ruled a county programme reached through an Esri endpoint is not Esri's basemap, and the evidence supports it — Okaloosa County serves this same imagery itself at county_service_url, verified by export. served_via is deliberately UNCHANGED: it records the channel this survey actually used, and imagery.geojson is a hand-surveyed record, so rewriting how it was made would falsify it rather than correct it. county_service_url is the admissible channel a re-survey or an ingest should use. (b) The deeper blocker is new: the raster is "flown in 2025 by Pictometry International Corp" — a vendor product the county licensed in, not a county work. Okaloosa GIS publishes "created by Okaloosa County GIS and is in the public domain pursuant to Chapter 119, Florida Statutes" on 13 vector items and zero imagery items across all 193 in its ArcGIS org; every imagery service publishes licenseInfo: "". Chapter 119 is a right of access, not a redistribution grant over a third party's copyrighted raster, so no licence class is recorded and none should be inferred from state law. (c) captured and horizontal_accuracy_m were both wrong and are corrected above. (d) sha256 stays null. Pin it from credentialed FTP tiles, not a server-side /export render, which is a derived product. Resolve (b) and (d) together with Okaloosa County GIS (webgis@myokaloosa.com). Coverage caveat: Eglin/Hurlburt AFB areas in this mosaic are 2013 9-inch fill.
